headline: Midjourney unveils full-body ultrasound scanner aiming for MRI-level detail in 60 seconds
summary: Midjourney, known for its AI image generator, has launched "The Midjourney Scanner," an ultrasound-based system designed to provide MRI-comparable full-body scans in just 60 seconds. It aims to analyze muscle, fat, bone, and organs without radiation.
details: Midjourney CEO David Holz revealed "The Midjourney Scanner," an ultrasound-based full-body scanner. This new hardware product aims for image quality comparable to MRI machines in many ways, completing a scan in about 60 seconds. It initially focuses on the composition of muscle, fat, bone, and organs.

Developed in partnership with Butterfly Network, the scanner utilizes 40 Butterfly Ultrasound-on-Chip imaging modules. Users step onto a platform that descends into water, passing through a ring of thousands of transducers that send and record ultrasonic waves to create detailed 3D images.

Holz envisions the scanner being used annually or even daily to track body changes in response to diet and exercise. The company's goal is to "bring safe, fast, and high fidelity preventative scanning to billions via a magical spa experience."

Future plans include opening a Midjourney Spa in San Francisco's Union Square by the end of 2027, housing 10 scanners. These spas will offer a holistic experience, combining scanning rooms with hot tubs, gyms, saunas, and cold plunges.

Currently, Midjourney Medical is focusing on "body composition maps," which do not require the same level of FDA clearance as diagnostic imaging. The company emphasizes data privacy, stating more details on policies will be released closer to launch.

Holz suggests these scans could eventually surpass MRI in certain aspects, offering detailed internal body insights "real fast" without radiation or powerful magnets. The collected "library of scans" can be shared with doctors or AI health tools.

topic: epic games open-sources lore version control system
headline_marked: [[Epic Games open-sources Lore]], a new VCS built in Rust for massive game assets
headline: Epic Games open-sources Lore, a new VCS built in Rust for massive game assets
summary: Lore is a centralized, content-addressed version control system designed to manage enormous binary files, battle-tested with Fortnite's UEFN toolkit.
details: Epic Games has released Lore as open-source, an MIT-licensed version control system written in Rust. It's specifically engineered to handle the massive binary files common in game development, such as 4K textures and 3D models, alongside source code.

Unlike Git, which is optimized for text, Lore addresses the limitations of existing VCS solutions like Git LFS and proprietary options like Perforce Helix Core. It offers a new approach for studios struggling with terabyte-scale repositories.

Lore's architecture uses content-addressed storage, where every data piece is referenced by its cryptographic hash. This ensures a tamper-evident history and allows for efficient storage by splitting large files into reusable chunks, only storing changed portions.

The system supports on-demand downloads, meaning developers only fetch the file data they need for their current task, significantly reducing local storage requirements and improving workflow speed. It also features lightweight, low-overhead branching.

While centralized like Perforce, Lore incorporates intelligent caching to scale throughput for large teams. It provides a full CLI interface and multi-language APIs (C/C++, C#, Rust, Go, Python, JavaScript) for extensive integration and custom tooling.

Currently at v0.8.3, Lore is pre-1.0 and under active development. The team notes that interfaces and APIs may change, and the UEFN build uses a proprietary compression format not yet in the open-source version.

Lore is ideal for game studios, film & VFX, and any enterprise software dealing with large binaries like ML models or datasets. Its open-source nature provides a free alternative to expensive proprietary systems, fostering community development.
